intent.raw_query: Hawaii family beach vacation, $5000, 10 days, August 2026 from Seattle

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most iconic marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish and sea turtles. Perfect for families with kids of all ages, the bay offers calm, shallow waters and equipment rentals on-site. An educational visitor center teaches about the reef ecosystem before you enter.
experiences.location: Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve, East Oahu

experiences.name: Luau Dinner Experience at Old Lahaina Luau
experiences.description: Immerse your family in authentic Hawaiian culture with a traditional luau featuring hula dancing, fire knife performances, and a feast of kalua pig, poi, and fresh tropical fruits. This award-winning luau is set on the oceanfront and is considered one of the most authentic in all of Hawaii, offering a magical sunset backdrop.

experiences.name: Waimea Canyon Hike and Lookout
experiences.description: Known as the 'Grand Canyon of the Pacific,' Waimea Canyon offers breathtaking views and family-friendly hiking trails through lush valleys and dramatic red-rock formations. Kids will love spotting native birds and waterfalls along the way. The Canyon Trail is manageable for most ages and rewards hikers with stunning panoramic vistas.

experiences.name: Shave Ice and Food Tour in Haleiwa Town
experiences.description: Stroll through the charming surf town of Haleiwa on Oahu's North Shore and indulge in Hawaii's legendary shave ice at Matsumoto's, a local institution since 1951. Sample fresh poke bowls, garlic shrimp from roadside trucks, and tropical smoothies. This laid-back town also offers boutique shopping and a peek into authentic Hawaiian surf culture.

experiences.name: Kaanapali Beach Family Day
experiences.description: Spend a full day at one of America's best beaches, featuring calm turquoise waters ideal for swimming, boogie boarding, and building sandcastles. Families can rent paddleboards and kayaks, watch cliff divers at Black Rock (Puu Kekaa), and enjoy beachside dining at casual restaurants along the famous Kaanapali Beach Walk. Sunsets here are absolutely spectacular.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Hawaii
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Waimea Canyon Hike and Lookout
experiences.description: Known as the 'Grand Canyon of the Pacific,' Waimea Canyon offers breathtaking views and family-friendly hiking trails through lush valleys and dramatic red-rock formations. Kids will love spotting native birds and waterfalls along the way. The Canyon Trail is manageable for most ages and rewards hikers with stunning panoramic vistas.

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Honolulu Airport at 22:30. Collect luggage, arrange ground transportation (TheBus route 20 is the most budget-friendly option at ~$3/person), and check in to Aegean Bliss Resort. Settle into your beachfront room and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or airport snacks
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport snacks
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night bite at 7-Eleven or ABC Stores near the airport (open 24 hours) — plate lunches and musubi available for under $5

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Pre-order a grocery delivery to the hotel (via Instacart or Amazon Fresh) so breakfast items are waiting in your room. Pack a light carry-on snack bag to avoid expensive airport food.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, walk directly to the beachfront outside Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy the free beach access, build sandcastles with the kids, and take a morning swim. Explore the shoreline and get oriented with your surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a nearby local beach park (look for the closest public beach park to your resort) for free family fun. Rent a boogie board from a local surf shack (~$10/day) and ride the waves. Many Hawaiian beach parks have free picnic tables and restrooms — perfect for families.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the beachfront at sunset. Visit a nearby ABC Store or local grocery (Times Supermarket or Foodland) to stock up on snacks, sunscreen, and drinks for the week. Watch the sunset from the beach — completely free and spectacular.

meals.breakfast: Eat from your pre-stocked groceries in the room — cereal, fruit, yogurt. Budget: ~$5/person
meals.lunch: Pick up spam musubi, manapua, or a plate lunch from a nearby local food truck or convenience store. Budget: ~$8–10/person
meals.dinner: Visit a local plate lunch spot or Hawaiian BBQ restaurant. Look for 'keiki meals' (kids' meals) for the little ones. Try Ono Hawaiian Foods or similar local spots. Budget: ~$12–15/person

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is intentionally relaxed to help the family adjust to the time zone difference. Hawaii is 2–3 hours behind the US West Coast and 5–6 hours behind the East Coast. Stay hydrated and apply sunscreen every 2 hours — the Hawaiian sun is intense even on cloudy days.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Diamond Head State Monument (if on Oahu). The hike is only $5/person (or $10/car) and takes about 1.5–2 hours round trip. The panoramic views from the summit crater are stunning and family-friendly. Start early (7:00–8:00 AM) to beat the heat and crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve for world-class snorkeling. Entry is $25/adult (free for children under 13). Rent snorkel gear on-site (~$15) or bring your own. The bay is a protected marine sanctuary teeming with sea turtles, colorful fish, and coral. Book your timed entry reservation online in advance — spots fill up fast.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and rinse off. Walk or drive to a nearby local farmers market or food truck park for dinner. Look for fresh poke bowls, plate lunches, and shave ice for dessert. Many markets are free to browse and offer affordable, authentic Hawaiian food.

meals.breakfast: Hotel room breakfast — toast, fruit, juice. Budget: ~$4/person
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from the grocery store — sandwiches, chips, fruit, and water — to eat at Hanauma Bay's picnic area. Budget: ~$6/person
meals.dinner: Local food truck or farmers market dinner. Poke bowl (~$12), plate lunch (~$10), shave ice dessert (~$4). Budget: ~$14–16/person

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay reservations are MANDATORY and must be booked online at least 2 days in advance at hawaiistateparks.org. The bay is closed on Tuesdays. If visiting on a Tuesday, swap this activity with Day 4's plan.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Polynesian Cultural Center (if budget allows — tickets start at ~$60/adult, $48/child) OR opt for the free alternative: explore Waimea Valley on Oahu (entry ~$20/adult, $10/child), which features a beautiful botanical garden, cultural exhibits, and a stunning waterfall the kids can swim in. The valley walk is easy and family-friendly.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Sunset Beach or Waimea Bay Beach Park on the North Shore. These iconic beaches are free to visit and offer incredible scenery. In August, the waters are typically calm and safe for swimming (big waves are a winter phenomenon). Let the kids play in the sand while you relax.
day_by_day.evening: Grab dinner at Giovanni's Shrimp Truck, one of the most famous and affordable food trucks on the North Shore (~$14–16 per plate). The garlic shrimp scampi is legendary. Eat at the picnic tables outside and enjoy the laid-back North Shore atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel room breakfast. Budget: ~$4/person
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from the grocery store to enjoy at Waimea Valley or the beach. Budget: ~$6/person
meals.dinner: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck or nearby North Shore food trucks. Budget: ~$14–16/person

day_by_day.notes: The North Shore is about a 45–60 minute drive from Waikiki. If renting a car, this is a great day for it. Alternatively, TheBus Route 52 (Circle Island) can get you there for just $3/person, though it takes longer. Bring cash — many North Shore food trucks are cash only.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Kailua Beach, consistently rated one of the best beaches in the US. The beach is free, features calm turquoise waters perfect for families, and offers kayak rentals (~$25–35/hour for a double kayak). Paddle out to the Mokulua Islands (the 'Mokes') for a memorable family adventure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through the charming Kailua Town. Browse local boutiques, pick up affordable souvenirs, and visit the Kailua Farmers Market (held on Thursdays and Sundays). Try a fresh açaí bowl or local pastry from a neighborhood café.
day_by_day.evening: Drive or bus back toward your resort. Stop at a local plate lunch restaurant for an affordable dinner. Try Rainbow Drive-In (a Honolulu institution since 1961) for classic Hawaiian comfort food at budget-friendly prices (~$9–12 per plate).

meals.breakfast: Hotel room breakfast. Budget: ~$4/person
meals.lunch: Kailua Town café or farmers market food stall — açaí bowls, sandwiches, or local snacks. Budget: ~$8–10/person
meals.dinner: Rainbow Drive-In or similar local plate lunch spot. Budget: ~$9–12/person

day_by_day.notes: Kailua is on the windward (east) side of Oahu and is about 30 minutes from Waikiki by car. On windy days, the kite surfing at Kailua Beach is spectacular to watch — free entertainment! Bring reef-safe sunscreen as Hawaii has banned oxybenzone-based sunscreens to protect coral reefs.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Pearl Harbor National Memorial. The grounds and exhibits are free to enter. The USS Arizona Memorial boat tour is also free (but requires a timed reservation — book at recreation.gov well in advance). This is a deeply moving and historically significant experience for older children and adults alike.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Battleship Missouri Memorial (~$32/adult, $16/child) or the Pacific Aviation Museum (~$25/adult, $15/child) for an additional immersive history experience. Alternatively, save money by sticking to the free Pearl Harbor Visitor Center exhibits and gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Ala Moana Center (the largest open-air mall in the US) for window shopping and dinner at the affordable food court. The food court has dozens of options including poke, ramen, Korean BBQ, and more — most plates run $8–12. Watch the free hula show performed at the Ala Moana stage on weekends.

meals.breakfast: Hotel room breakfast. Budget: ~$4/person
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from the grocery store to eat at Pearl Harbor's picnic area, or grab a quick bite from the on-site café. Budget: ~$6–8/person
meals.dinner: Ala Moana Center food court. Budget: ~$8–12/person

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor is extremely popular — arrive early (doors open at 7:00 AM) even with a reservation. The Arizona Memorial boat tour fills up months in advance, so book as soon as possible. Children under 3 are not permitted on the Arizona Memorial boat for safety reasons.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to experience the Waimea Canyon Hike and Lookout (the 'Grand Canyon of the Pacific') on Kauai — OR if staying on Oahu, visit the Manoa Falls Trail. Manoa Falls is a stunning 150-foot waterfall accessible via a 1.6-mile round-trip hike through a lush rainforest. Entry is $5/person for parking; the trail itself is free. The hike is easy to moderate and great for families.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hike, visit Lyon Arboretum (free, donations welcome) adjacent to Manoa Valley for a peaceful stroll through tropical gardens. Alternatively, head to Waikiki Beach for the afternoon — one of the most famous beaches in the world and completely free. Try a beginner surf lesson (~$25–35/person for a group lesson).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the Waikiki sunset from the beach. Walk along Kalakaua Avenue and enjoy the free street entertainment — hula dancers, musicians, and fire performers often perform near the beachfront. Grab dinner from a local spot off the main strip to avoid tourist-trap pricing.

meals.breakfast: Hotel room breakfast. Budget: ~$4/person
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch for the hike — sandwiches, trail mix, and plenty of water. Budget: ~$6/person
meals.dinner: Waikiki side-street restaurant or food truck. Try Marugame Udon (affordable Japanese udon) or Me BBQ for Korean-Hawaiian fusion. Budget: ~$10–14/person

day_by_day.notes: The Manoa Falls Trail can be muddy — wear closed-toe shoes and bring a light rain jacket. Do not swim in the Manoa Falls pool as there is a risk of leptospirosis from the freshwater. If planning the Kauai day trip instead, book a short inter-island flight (Hawaiian Airlines or Southwest) well in advance for the best budget fares (~$80–120 round trip).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Honolulu Zoo (located in Waikiki) — tickets are ~$19/adult and $11/child, making it one of the most affordable family attractions in Waikiki. The zoo is home to African savanna animals, tropical birds, and a great children's zoo section. Arrive early when animals are most active.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk directly from the zoo to Waikiki Aquarium (~$12/adult, $5/child) for an up-close look at Hawaiian marine life, including monk seals, jellyfish, and vibrant reef fish. Both attractions are within easy walking distance of each other.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost luau preview or cultural show. The Kuhio Beach Hula Show is held every Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday at sunset at Kuhio Beach Park — it's completely FREE and features authentic hula dancing and torch lighting. Don't miss it!

meals.breakfast: Hotel room breakfast. Budget: ~$4/person
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch to eat at the zoo's picnic area. Budget: ~$6/person
meals.dinner: Grab plate lunches or poke bowls from a nearby local restaurant before the hula show. Budget: ~$10–12/person

day_by_day.notes: The Kuhio Beach Hula Show is one of Hawaii's best free experiences and is perfect for families. Check the schedule at honolulu.gov/parks for exact times as they can vary seasonally. Bring a blanket to sit on the grass and arrive 20–30 minutes early for a good spot.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning at Lanikai Beach (near Kailua) for one of the most beautiful and uncrowded beach experiences in Hawaii. The beach is free and features powdery white sand and stunning views of the Mokulua Islands. Great for a final family beach day — swimming, snorkeling, and relaxing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or bus the Pali Highway and stop at the Nu'uanu Pali Lookout — a breathtaking cliffside viewpoint with sweeping views of the windward coast. Entry is $7/car or free if you walk in. The wind at the lookout is famously intense — hold on to the kids! Then explore the nearby Byodo-In Temple in the Valley of the Temples (~$5/adult, $2/child), a stunning replica of a Japanese temple set against dramatic green cliffs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a final beach sunset. Pack your bags and do any last-minute souvenir shopping at ABC Stores (budget-friendly souvenirs) or local markets. Enjoy a farewell dinner at a beloved local spot.

meals.breakfast: Hotel room breakfast. Budget: ~$4/person
meals.lunch: Pack a beach picnic from the grocery store. Budget: ~$6/person
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a local Hawaiian restaurant. Try Helena's Hawaiian Food (a James Beard Award-winning institution) for authentic, affordable Hawaiian cuisine. Budget: ~$12–15/person

day_by_day.notes: Helena's Hawaiian Food is a Honolulu legend and very affordable for the quality. It's cash only and can have a line — arrive early. For souvenirs, skip the Waikiki tourist shops and head to local craft fairs or Aloha Stadium Swap Meet (held on Wednesdays, Saturdays, and Sundays for $1 entry) for the best prices on local goods.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for one final sunrise walk on the beach outside Aegean Bliss Resort. Take photos, collect a few shells as free souvenirs, and soak in the last moments of paradise. Check out of the hotel (most checkouts are by 11:00 AM — confirm with the resort).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, visit a nearby attraction for a final activity — the Iolani Palace (the only royal palace in the US, ~$22/adult, $6/child) in downtown Honolulu is a worthwhile final stop. Alternatively, browse Chinatown Honolulu for affordable last-minute gifts and snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Daniel K. Inouye International Airport. Allow at least 2–3 hours before departure for check-in and security. Grab a final meal at the airport — Panda Express or local vendors in the terminal are more affordable than sit-down restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel room breakfast or grab a quick bite from a nearby café. Budget: ~$4–6/person
meals.lunch: Chinatown Honolulu food stalls or a local plate lunch spot near the airport. Budget: ~$8–10/person
meals.dinner: Airport terminal food options. Budget: ~$10–15/person

day_by_day.notes: Hawaii's agricultural inspection is strict — you cannot bring most fresh fruits, plants, or certain food items back to the mainland US. Check the USDA guidelines before packing your bags. Pre-packaged macadamia nuts, Kona coffee, and commercially prepared foods are generally fine to bring home. Mahalo for visiting Hawaii — a hui hou (until we meet again)!

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at airport at 22:30. Collect luggage, arrange ground transportation or rental car, and check in to Aegean Bliss Resort Beachfront. Settle into your room and enjoy a light welcome drink at the resort bar if still open.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at departure airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at departure airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the airport upon arrival or order room service at the resort to unwind after the long flight

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — focus on arriving safely and getting a good night's rest. Confirm resort check-in details in advance as you arrive late at night. Pack a carry-on snack bag for the flight to avoid hunger on arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. After breakfast, take a relaxed walk along the beachfront to get your bearings. Spend time on the resort beach — swim, build sandcastles with the family, and soak in your first full Hawaiian morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kaanapali Beach Family Day — spend the afternoon at one of America's most celebrated beaches. Enjoy calm turquoise waters perfect for swimming, try a beginner snorkel session in the shallows, and rent paddleboards or boogie boards from a beach vendor for family fun.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll the Kaanapali Boardwalk and watch the famous cliff diving ceremony at Black Rock (Pu'u Keka'a) at sunset — a free and spectacular local tradition. Head to a nearby casual beachside restaurant for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet at Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy fresh tropical fruits, eggs, and local pastries
meals.lunch: Beachside food truck or casual café near Kaanapali Beach — try a plate lunch with kalua pork, rice, and macaroni salad (~$12–$18 per person)
meals.dinner: Leilani's on the Beach, Kaanapali — mid-range oceanfront dining with fresh fish tacos, burgers, and Hawaiian-inspired plates (~$20–$35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Apply reef-safe sunscreen generously — the Hawaiian sun is strong even on overcast days. Bring water shoes for the rocky sections near Black Rock. This is a great gentle reintroduction day after travel.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning snorkeling adventure at Hanauma Bay — one of Hawaii's most iconic marine sanctuaries. Arrive early (before 9:00 AM) to secure entry as daily visitor numbers are capped. Watch the mandatory marine education video, then explore the crystal-clear bay teeming with sea turtles, parrotfish, and vibrant coral.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive along the scenic coastline back toward the resort. Stop at a local shave ice stand for a refreshing treat. Spend the mid-afternoon relaxing at the resort pool or beach, allowing kids time to play freely.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset from the resort beachfront. Have dinner at a local mid-range Hawaiian restaurant nearby.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort or grab a granola bar and fruit before the early Hanauma Bay departure — the bay opens early and entry fills up fast
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch near Hanauma Bay — pack sandwiches and fruit, or grab plate lunches from a nearby deli to eat at the bay's picnic area
meals.dinner: Mama's Fish House or a similar local seafood restaurant near the resort — known for fresh catch-of-the-day dishes (~$30–$50 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance reservations online — book at least 2 days ahead. Entry fee is approximately $25 per adult; children under 12 are free. Snorkel gear can be rented on-site. Reef-safe sunscreen is mandatory at the bay.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Haleiwa Town on Oahu's North Shore for the Shave Ice and Food Tour. Stroll the charming surf town, browse local boutiques and art galleries, and stop at the legendary Matsumoto Shave Ice for Hawaii's most famous frozen treat with tropical syrups and mochi.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the North Shore beaches — watch professional surfers (August may have moderate surf) at Sunset Beach or Waimea Bay. Let kids play in the calmer shore breaks. Visit the Dole Pineapple Plantation on the way back for a fun family stop — enjoy Dole Whip and a pineapple garden maze.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and relax. Enjoy dinner at a local restaurant near the resort with a Hawaiian fusion menu.

meals.breakfast: Kono's Northshore in Haleiwa — famous for breakfast burritos with kalua pork and eggs, a beloved local spot (~$10–$15 per person)
meals.lunch: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck, Haleiwa — iconic North Shore food truck serving garlic butter shrimp plates (~$15 per plate)
meals.dinner: Haleiwa Joe's Seafood Grill — mid-range casual dining with fresh seafood, burgers, and Hawaiian plates in a relaxed setting (~$20–$35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The North Shore is about a 45–60 minute drive depending on your resort location. Start the morning early to avoid traffic. The Dole Plantation charges a small entry fee for the maze (~$8 per person) but the grounds are free to explore. Haleiwa is very family-friendly.

day_by_day.morning: Take a scenic drive to Waimea Canyon — known as the 'Grand Canyon of the Pacific.' Begin with the Waimea Canyon Lookout for breathtaking panoramic views. Choose a family-friendly trail such as the Canyon Trail (1.8 miles round trip) for a manageable hike with stunning red-rock vistas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving up to the Kalalau Lookout at Kokee State Park for views of the dramatic Na Pali Coast cliffs and valleys. Browse the small Kokee Natural History Museum. Begin the scenic drive back down, stopping at roadside fruit stands for fresh local produce.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and enjoy a quiet evening. Treat the family to a sunset beach walk and a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Pack a hearty breakfast from the resort or stop at a local bakery on the way — you'll want energy for hiking
meals.lunch: Kokee Lodge Restaurant near the canyon — casual diner-style lunch with burgers, soups, and local plates (~$12–$18 per person)
meals.dinner: Keoki's Paradise, Poipu — mid-range Hawaiian restaurant with a tropical garden atmosphere, fresh fish, and family-friendly menu (~$25–$40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Waimea Canyon is on Kauai — if your resort is on Maui or Oahu, this may require an inter-island flight or ferry. Plan accordingly and consider booking a day trip package. Wear sturdy closed-toe shoes for hiking. Bring layers as it gets cooler at higher elevations. Bring plenty of water.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a free morning at the resort — sleep in, swim in the pool, or explore the resort amenities. This is a deliberate rest day mid-trip to recharge. Let kids enjoy the beach freely while adults relax with a book or spa treatment if available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local Hawaiian cultural center or aquarium near the resort. The Maui Ocean Center (if on Maui) is a world-class family attraction featuring a walk-through shark tunnel, sea turtle lagoon, and interactive exhibits — perfect for all ages.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the Luau Dinner Experience at Old Lahaina Luau — an unforgettable evening of authentic Hawaiian culture featuring traditional hula dancing, fire knife performances, imu-roasted kalua pig, and a lavish Hawaiian buffet. This is a highlight of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Relaxed resort breakfast — take your time and enjoy the full spread
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort pool bar or a nearby casual café — fish tacos, wraps, or a fresh poke bowl (~$15–$20 per person)
meals.dinner: Included in the Old Lahaina Luau experience — a full Hawaiian feast with kalua pig, poi, lomi salmon, haupia dessert, and tropical drinks (~$130–$160 per adult, ~$80–$100 per child)

day_by_day.notes: Old Lahaina Luau is extremely popular — book tickets at least 3–4 weeks in advance. The luau typically begins at sunset (around 5:30–6:00 PM) and lasts 2.5–3 hours. Arrive 30 minutes early for lei greeting and pre-show activities. This is a must-do family memory.

day_by_day.morning: Morning snorkel or paddleboard session directly from the resort beachfront. Many beachfront resorts offer gear rentals on-site. Explore the reef just offshore and look for sea turtles, which are common in Hawaiian coastal waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a family whale watching or dolphin watching boat tour (seasonal, but spinner dolphins are present year-round in Hawaii). Many tours depart from local harbors and last 2–3 hours. Kids will love spotting dolphins bow-riding the boat.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local farmers market or night market if available in the area. Pick up fresh tropical fruits, local honey, and Hawaiian snacks. Enjoy a casual dinner at a nearby restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or a local café — açaí bowls with fresh mango, granola, and coconut are a Hawaiian staple (~$12–$16)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from a local grocery store (Foodland or Times Supermarket) to enjoy on the boat tour or at the harbor
meals.dinner: Down to Earth or a local Hawaiian BBQ restaurant — try huli huli chicken, macaroni salad, and steamed rice for an authentic local experience (~$15–$25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the dolphin/whale watching tour in advance. Morning tours tend to have calmer seas and better wildlife sightings. Apply motion sickness patches or medication the night before if any family members are prone to seasickness. Bring a light jacket for the boat.

day_by_day.morning: Explore a local botanical garden or nature preserve near the resort. Hawaii's lush tropical flora is stunning — options include the Allerton Garden (Kauai), Kepaniwai Heritage Gardens (Maui), or Lyon Arboretum (Oahu). A peaceful, educational morning walk through tropical plants, koi ponds, and cultural heritage displays.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local beach different from your usual spots — try a less-crowded hidden gem recommended by resort staff. Spend the afternoon snorkeling, collecting shells, and simply enjoying the Hawaiian coastline at a slower pace.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a family cooking class or Hawaiian cultural workshop — many resorts and local studios offer lei-making, ukulele lessons, or hula classes for families. A fun, hands-on evening activity that creates lasting memories.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery or café — try Portuguese malasadas (Hawaiian doughnuts) from a local Leonard's Bakery outlet or similar (~$8–$12 per person)
meals.lunch: Casual beachside lunch — fresh poke bowl from a local poke shop, a Hawaiian staple that's fresh, healthy, and delicious (~$14–$18 per person)
meals.dinner: Mid-range local restaurant with ocean views — try fresh ahi tuna, grilled mahi-mahi, or a Hawaiian mixed plate (~$25–$40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Check resort concierge for cultural activity schedules — many resorts offer complimentary or low-cost lei-making and ukulele sessions for guests. Botanical gardens often have discounted family rates. This is a wonderful day to slow down and connect with Hawaiian culture.

day_by_day.morning: Last full adventure day — start with an early morning sunrise hike to a scenic viewpoint. Options include Diamond Head Crater (Oahu), Lahaina Pali Trail (Maui), or the Sleeping Giant Trail (Kauai) depending on your location. Moderate difficulty, spectacular views, and a rewarding family achievement.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Kaanapali Beach or your favorite beach from the trip for one final full afternoon of swimming, snorkeling, and beach games. Let the kids play freely and soak in every last moment of the Hawaiian sun and water.
day_by_day.evening: Special farewell dinner at a nicer restaurant to celebrate the end of a wonderful trip. Dress up slightly and enjoy a memorable Hawaiian dining experience as a family.

meals.breakfast: Grab-and-go breakfast before the sunrise hike — pack energy bars, bananas, and water bottles the night before
meals.lunch: Post-hike reward at a local restaurant or food truck — celebrate the hike with a hearty plate lunch or fresh fish sandwich (~$15–$20 per person)
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at a well-regarded local restaurant — try Merriman's Maui, Alan Wong's, or a comparable upscale-casual spot with fresh Hawaiian Regional Cuisine (~$45–$65 per person)

day_by_day.notes: For sunrise hikes, wake up by 4:30–5:00 AM and depart by 5:00 AM. Bring headlamps, water, and snacks. Diamond Head requires advance online reservations. This is a great day to buy final souvenirs — local macadamia nuts, Kona coffee, and Hawaiian sea salt make wonderful gifts.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take one last walk on the beach and collect any special shells or photos. Pack bags and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort — store luggage with the concierge if your flight is in the afternoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time, spend remaining hours at the resort pool or nearby beach. Pick up any last-minute souvenirs at a local gift shop or airport duty-free. Head to the airport with plenty of time — aim to arrive 2.5–3 hours before international/mainland departure.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Hawaii with incredible family memories, a sun-kissed glow, and hearts full of aloha spirit.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — savor the tropical fruits, fresh juices, and ocean views one last time
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the resort or at the airport — grab a final poke bowl or plate lunch before boarding (~$15–$20 per person)
meals.dinner: On the plane or at a connecting airport

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 AM — confirm with the resort. Ask the concierge to store luggage if your flight departs in the evening. Hawaii airport security can be busy in summer — allow extra time. Don't forget to declare any agricultural items (fruits, plants) that cannot leave Hawaii. Mahalo for a wonderful trip!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Hawaii Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most iconic marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish and sea turtles. Perfect for families with kids of all ages, the bay offers calm, shallow waters and equipment rentals on-site. An educational visitor center teaches about the reef ecosystem before you enter.
experiences.location: Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve, East Oahu

experiences.name: Luau Dinner Experience at Old Lahaina Luau
experiences.description: Immerse your family in authentic Hawaiian culture with a traditional luau featuring hula dancing, fire knife performances, and a feast of kalua pig, poi, and fresh tropical fruits. This award-winning luau is set on the oceanfront and is considered one of the most authentic in all of Hawaii, offering a magical sunset backdrop.

experiences.name: Waimea Canyon Hike and Lookout
experiences.description: Known as the 'Grand Canyon of the Pacific,' Waimea Canyon offers breathtaking views and family-friendly hiking trails through lush valleys and dramatic red-rock formations. Kids will love spotting native birds and waterfalls along the way. The Canyon Trail is manageable for most ages and rewards hikers with stunning panoramic vistas.

experiences.name: Shave Ice and Food Tour in Haleiwa Town
experiences.description: Stroll through the charming surf town of Haleiwa on Oahu's North Shore and indulge in Hawaii's legendary shave ice at Matsumoto's, a local institution since 1951. Sample fresh poke bowls, garlic shrimp from roadside trucks, and tropical smoothies. This laid-back town also offers boutique shopping and a peek into authentic Hawaiian surf culture.

experiences.name: Kaanapali Beach Family Day
experiences.description: Spend a full day at one of America's best beaches, featuring calm turquoise waters ideal for swimming, boogie boarding, and building sandcastles. Families can rent paddleboards and kayaks, watch cliff divers at Black Rock (Puu Kekaa), and enjoy beachside dining at casual restaurants along the famous Kaanapali Beach Walk. Sunsets here are absolutely spectacular.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Honolulu Airport at 22:30 via Flight UA. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in to your Beachfront suite, enjoy a welcome amenity prepared by the resort (tropical fruit platter, champagne, and fresh lei greeting). Settle in and rest.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit
meals.dinner: Light late-night room service at the resort — recommended: fresh poke bowl, island fruit, and herbal tea to ease into Hawaiian time

day_by_day.notes: Confirm private airport transfer in advance. Request early check-in amenities and a resort orientation packet at the front desk. Keep the first night light to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely resort morning — enjoy a premium breakfast at the resort's oceanfront restaurant. Take a private guided orientation walk along the beachfront property, get acquainted with resort amenities including the infinity pool, cabanas, and water sports desk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kaanapali Beach Family Day — spend the afternoon at one of America's most celebrated beaches just steps from the resort. Enjoy calm turquoise waters perfect for swimming, rent premium snorkel gear through the resort, build sandcastles, and relax under a private cabana with butler service.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's beachfront bar. Enjoy a curated tasting menu dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant, featuring locally sourced Hawaiian seafood and farm-to-table ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Oceanfront breakfast at the resort — fresh açaí bowls, eggs Benedict with kalua pork, tropical juices, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Beachside cabana service — gourmet sandwiches, fresh ceviche, coconut water, and shave ice delivered to your cabana
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant — multi-course tasting menu featuring Hamachi crudo, macadamia-crusted mahi-mahi, and lilikoi cheesecake for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Reserve a premium beachfront cabana in advance through the resort concierge. Sunscreen and reef-safe products are strongly recommended. This is a gentle reintroduction day — keep the pace relaxed.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay — depart early (7:00 AM recommended) via private chauffeured vehicle to beat the crowds. Explore one of Hawaii's most iconic marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish, sea turtles, and vibrant coral. A private guide ensures a premium, educational experience for the whole family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a poolside lunch. Afternoon at leisure — enjoy the resort's spa for adults while kids participate in the resort's supervised children's program or water activities at the pool.
day_by_day.evening: Private beachfront bonfire experience arranged through the resort concierge — roast marshmallows, enjoy live ukulele music, and stargaze over the Pacific. Followed by an intimate dinner at a premium oceanfront restaurant nearby.

meals.breakfast: Early continental breakfast at the resort before departure — pastries, fresh fruit, yogurt parfait, and Kona coffee to go
meals.lunch: Poolside gourmet lunch at the resort — fresh lobster rolls, grilled shrimp tacos, tropical smoothies
meals.dinner: Roy's Hawaii Kai or equivalent upscale restaurant — known for Euro-Asian cuisine; try the misoyaki butterfish and molten chocolate soufflé

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance reservations and charges a conservation fee. Arrive early as entry is capped daily. Bring reef-safe sunscreen only — chemical sunscreen is prohibited to protect the coral reef.

day_by_day.morning: Shave Ice and Food Tour in Haleiwa Town — private chauffeured excursion to Oahu's legendary North Shore surf town. Stroll through charming boutiques, visit the iconic Matsumoto Shave Ice, sample local food trucks, fresh poke, and artisan treats. A guided food tour adds context and insider access to the best hidden gems.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the North Shore — watch professional surfers ride the famous waves at Waimea Bay or Sunset Beach (conditions permitting in August). Visit the Dole Plantation for a family-friendly pineapple garden maze and premium tasting experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a relaxed evening. Enjoy a private in-suite dinner arranged by the resort — a personal chef prepares a Hawaiian feast in your suite with fresh local ingredients, paired with curated Hawaiian wines.

meals.breakfast: In-suite breakfast delivered — fluffy macadamia nut pancakes, fresh papaya, scrambled eggs, and fresh-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Haleiwa food tour tasting lunch — shave ice, garlic shrimp plates from Giovanni's Shrimp Truck, fresh poke bowls, and tropical fruit
meals.dinner: Private in-suite chef experience — Hawaiian-themed 4-course dinner: taro soup, fresh island salad, grilled opah fish, and haupia coconut pudding

day_by_day.notes: Book the private in-suite chef experience at least 48 hours in advance through the resort concierge. The North Shore is about 1 hour from most resort areas — confirm transportation timing. August surf is generally calmer on the North Shore, making it safe and scenic for families.

day_by_day.morning: Luau Dinner Experience prep day — morning begins with a private catamaran sailing excursion along the coastline. Enjoy snorkeling, dolphin watching, and a champagne brunch on deck while gliding along the crystal-blue Pacific. A premium sailing company provides full service including gear, towels, and gourmet food.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to resort for relaxation — spa treatments for adults (lomi lomi massage, volcanic stone therapy) while children enjoy the resort kids' club with Hawaiian craft activities, hula lessons, and supervised pool time.
day_by_day.evening: Luau Dinner Experience at Old Lahaina Luau — immerse the family in authentic Hawaiian culture with a traditional luau featuring hula dancing, fire knife performances, imu (underground oven) pig roast, and an elaborate feast of traditional Hawaiian dishes. One of Hawaii's most celebrated cultural experiences.

meals.breakfast: Champagne brunch on the private catamaran — smoked salmon, tropical fruit, croissants, mimosas (juice for kids), and freshly made omelets
meals.lunch: Light resort poolside lunch upon return — acai bowls, fresh sushi rolls, and coconut water
meals.dinner: Old Lahaina Luau feast — kalua pig, poi, lomi lomi salmon, haupia, fresh pineapple, and tropical cocktails included with the luau experience

day_by_day.notes: Old Lahaina Luau is extremely popular and books out weeks in advance — reserve immediately through the concierge. The luau typically begins at sunset (around 5:30–6:00 PM). Arrange private transport to and from the venue. Dress code is resort casual — light layers recommended for the evening breeze.

day_by_day.morning: Helicopter tour of the island — a premium sunrise helicopter excursion offering breathtaking aerial views of volcanic craters, lush valleys, hidden waterfalls, and the dramatic Na Pali Coastline (if visiting Kauai) or Diamond Head and the Oahu coastline. A truly unforgettable family experience with a private charter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Polynesian Cultural Center (if on Oahu) — a world-class cultural attraction featuring six authentic Polynesian villages, live demonstrations of traditional crafts, canoe rides, and interactive cultural experiences. Premium packages include VIP seating and behind-the-scenes access.
day_by_day.evening: Elegant resort dinner at a Forbes Five-Star-level restaurant — dress up for a sophisticated evening celebrating the midpoint of the trip. Choose a restaurant renowned for its wine list and locally inspired tasting menus.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before the helicopter tour — granola, fresh fruit, and coffee at the resort lobby café
meals.lunch: Polynesian Cultural Center — premium dining package included with VIP admission featuring traditional Polynesian dishes and island beverages
meals.dinner: Nobu Honolulu or equivalent luxury dining — black cod with miso, wagyu beef, and premium sake pairing; reservations essential

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter tours require weight and age minimums — confirm all family members qualify when booking. Book the Polynesian Cultural Center's Ali'i Luau and Gateway Buffet VIP package well in advance. This is a high-activity day — consider lighter scheduling if traveling with very young children.

day_by_day.morning: Inter-island flight or excursion to Kauai — depart on a short premium inter-island flight to the Garden Isle for a day trip. Upon arrival, begin with a scenic drive along the Waimea Canyon Lookout Road with a private naturalist guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Waimea Canyon Hike and Lookout — explore the 'Grand Canyon of the Pacific' with family-friendly trail options. The canyon stretches 10 miles long and over 3,600 feet deep with stunning red and green vistas. A private guide leads the family on a curated hike appropriate for all ages, sharing geological and cultural history along the way.
day_by_day.evening: Return flight to Oahu. Arrive back at the resort for a relaxed evening — enjoy the resort's outdoor jacuzzi, night swimming in the heated pool, and a casual but elegant dinner at the resort's second restaurant or beach bar.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure — eggs your way, fresh Hawaiian bread, tropical fruit plate, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch prepared by the resort and enjoyed at the Waimea Canyon Lookout — gourmet sandwiches, local cheeses, fresh fruit, and sparkling water with canyon views
meals.dinner: Resort beach bar dinner — premium burgers with truffle fries, fresh fish tacos, island cocktails, and a relaxed family atmosphere under the stars

day_by_day.notes: Waimea Canyon is on Kauai — this requires an inter-island flight (approximately 30–40 minutes) or can be substituted with a day trip via private charter plane for a more luxurious experience. Wear comfortable closed-toe shoes for the canyon hike. Layers recommended as the canyon rim can be cooler than sea level.

day_by_day.morning: Private surf lesson on the beach — a professional surf instructor provides a private family surf lesson on a beginner-friendly beach break. Equipment, rash guards, and reef-safe sunscreen provided. This is a quintessential Hawaiian experience suitable for all ages and skill levels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relaxed beach afternoon at the resort — build on the morning's surf skills, enjoy stand-up paddleboarding, kayaking, or simply lounge in a premium beachfront cabana. Children can enjoy supervised sandcastle building and junior water sports with the resort's activities team.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner cruise — board a luxury catamaran for a two-hour sunset dinner cruise along the coastline. Enjoy a gourmet four-course dinner, live Hawaiian music, and dramatic Pacific sunset views. Champagne toast included.

meals.breakfast: Beachfront breakfast at the resort — smoothie bowls, avocado toast with fresh ahi, pastries, and tropical juices
meals.lunch: Beachside resort service — fresh grilled fish, premium salads, coconut shrimp, and fresh-pressed lemonades at the cabana
meals.dinner: Luxury sunset dinner cruise — four-course menu featuring island salad, lobster bisque, grilled catch of the day, and chocolate lava cake with ocean views

day_by_day.notes: Book the sunset dinner cruise well in advance as premium vessels fill quickly. Confirm age requirements for children. Bring a light wrap or jacket for the evening breeze on the water. The surf lesson should be booked through the resort's water sports concierge for vetted, insured instructors.

day_by_day.morning: Pearl Harbor and USS Arizona Memorial — a deeply moving and historically significant experience for the family. Arrange a premium guided tour with a private historian for an in-depth, age-appropriate exploration of this iconic national monument. Includes the USS Bowfin Submarine Museum and the Battleship Missouri.
day_by_day.afternoon: Shopping and leisure at Ala Moana Center — the largest open-air shopping center in the world, featuring luxury brands, local Hawaiian designers, and gourmet food options. Pick up premium souvenirs, local art, and Hawaiian specialty products. Visit the nearby Waikiki Beach for a final afternoon swim.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell family celebration dinner — reserve a private dining room at one of Honolulu's most prestigious restaurants for a memorable final full-evening dinner. Surprise the family with a custom dessert and keepsake menu printed by the restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departure to Pearl Harbor — full American breakfast with local touches: Portuguese sausage, macadamia nut waffles, fresh island fruit
meals.lunch: Ala Moana area — MW Restaurant or Senia for an elevated lunch experience featuring Hawaii regional cuisine with farm-fresh ingredients
meals.dinner: La Mer at Halekulani Hotel — Honolulu's most acclaimed fine-dining restaurant featuring classic French cuisine with Hawaiian influences; prix-fixe tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor requires advance ticket reservations — the USS Arizona Memorial boat tour often sells out. The experience is respectful and solemn; prepare children appropriately. La Mer has a formal dress code — smart resort wear or business casual attire required. Request a window table for harbor views when making reservations.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise beach walk — wake early for a peaceful last sunrise stroll along the beachfront. Collect shells, take family photos, and soak in the last moments of paradise. Optional: a final swim or snorkel session in the calm morning waters before checkout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Resort checkout — late checkout (arrange with concierge in advance for a 2:00 PM checkout). Enjoy one final poolside lunch at the resort. Private luxury transfer to Honolulu Airport for departure. Use remaining time to browse duty-free Hawaiian specialty shops at the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — board flight home with beautiful memories, premium souvenirs, and the warmth of aloha spirit.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — indulge in your favorite dishes from the trip; treat the family to a special order of macadamia nut French toast, fresh tropical platters, and Kona coffee one last time
meals.lunch: Final poolside lunch at the resort — light and fresh: sushi rolls, fresh fruit, coconut water, and a celebratory virgin piña colada for the kids
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight — pack premium snacks from the resort or airport gourmet shops for the journey home

day_by_day.notes: Request a late checkout at least 48 hours in advance to ensure availability. Confirm private airport transfer timing based on your departure flight. Allow extra time at the airport for check-in and duty-free shopping. Ask the resort to prepare a farewell amenity or keepsake for the family — many luxury properties offer this as a standard gesture.
